analysis: The changed hunk in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~2172-2184) is documentation-only. It describes Flint constrained-decode chaining: FlintNativeProtocolConstraint and FlintAnswerStopConstraint opt into CBv2 constrained chaining, with redraw from retained logits and a maskCacheKey based on constraint state. It also puts RecursiveSI/flint-int4 on the automatic paged list, so it starts at the legacy serving width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra. The two supplied units (head text lines 798-1209 and 1210-1628) are unchanged surrounding context and do not include the changed lines, so I could not inspect the hunk in context. I examined the patch excerpt and the surrounding text against the threat model. No source, authentication, attestation, encryption, cache-storage or coordinator-contract change is present. The doc claims the token stream is identical to unchained decode and that a device mask is cached per state. If the implementation does not match, this could affect T-041-style cache or timing behavior, or T-029/T-010 resource handling. That would be an implementation question outside the supplied evidence, not a regression shown by this PR. The paged-list addition widens concurrency only on the high-end chips. This is governed by existing memory/KV admission and the configured width, and it does not touch the A-001 confidentiality boundary. Remaining integration question: if the code changes accompany this doc, check that the mask cache keyed by constraint state holds no prompt-derived data persisted to disk or shared across requests in a way that violates the T-041 salt-scoping posture. Also check that redraw preserves the per-row RNG and penalty state. This PR provides no evidence of either problem.
